title: Unipolar Neuron Networks Trained by Recirculation for Reward-Based Continual Learning
abstract: arXiv:2611.14153v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Unipolar neurons are the predominant type of nerve cell in the octopus and in most other invertebrates. A single neurite (a fiber extending from the cell body) branches into a tree that carries both input and output synapses. The branches send graded local outputs to nearby cells, and one site on the main neurite sends a global output to distant targets. This paper proposes a network of such neurons and a learning rule for it. Each neuron is modeled as a tree of passive segments, whose activations are computed exactly as the steady state of a linear system. The network learns from reward alone, with a rule called recirculation. After each forward pass, a second pass sends requested changes of the outputs back through the same connections. Each synapse then adjusts its weight using only quantities available at its own location. translated_title: 通过再循环训练的单极神经元网络用于基于奖励的持续学习
translated_abstract: 单极神经元是章鱼及大多数其他无脊椎动物中占主导地位的神经细胞类型。单一的神经突（从细胞体延伸出的纤维）分支成一棵树状结构，同时承载输入和输出突触。这些分支向附近的细胞发送分级的局部输出，而主神经突上的一个位点向远处的目标发送全局输出。本文提出了一种由这类神经元构成的网络及其学习规则。每个神经元被建模为由无源片段组成的树，其激活值作为线性系统的稳态被精确计算。该网络仅凭奖励信号进行学习，采用一种称为“再循环”（recirculation）的规则。每次前向传播之后，第二次传播将所请求的输出变化通过相同的连接反向送回。随后，每个突触仅利用其自身位置可获得的量来调整权重。由于每个神经元的系统是对称的，这种更新紧密遵循（上游）误差的梯度……
tldr: 该论文受章鱼等无脊椎动物单极神经元结构启发，提出了一种树状神经元网络，通过仅需奖励信号的“再循环”学习规则实现持续学习，其中每个突触仅依赖局部信息更新权重，且更新方向近似遵循误差梯度。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a network of octopus-inspired unipolar neurons modeled as trees, which learns from reward alone via a local "recirculation" rule, where each synapse updates using only locally available quantities in a way that closely follows the error gradient, enabling reward-based continual learning.
